answers.reasoning: The 2017 amendment to the Indian Forest Act, 1927 removed bamboo from the definition of 'tree' only where it grows on non-forest land; bamboo grown inside forest areas continues to be treated as a tree and cannot be freely felled, so statement 1 is false. Section 2(i) of the Forest Rights Act, 2006 expressly includes bamboo within 'minor forest produce', so statement 2 is true. Section 3(1)(c) of the same Act confers on forest dwellers the right of ownership, access to collect, use and dispose of minor forest produce, so statement 3 is true. Of the two options that exclude the false statement 1, only B also includes the true statement 2.

answers.value: Article 21 — the right to marry a person of one's choice is read into the right to life and personal liberty
answers.reasoning: The Supreme Court has held in Lata Singh, Shakti Vahini and Shafin Jahan (the Hadiya case) that the choice of a life partner is intrinsic to the dignity and personal liberty guaranteed by Article 21, and that neither the State nor family may interfere with an adult's marital choice. Article 19 covers the six freedoms of speech, assembly, association, movement, residence and profession; Article 25 covers freedom of religion; Article 29 protects the cultural and educational interests of minorities — none of these is the source of the right in question.

Plant varieties are protected instead under the sui generis Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers' Rights Act, 2001. The Intellectual Property Appellate Board was constituted in 2003 and was functioning at the time of this paper (it was abolished only in 2021), so statement 2 is false. Only option C names statement 3 alone.

Statement 1 rests on the wide enabling power in Section 3(1) read with the rule-making power in Section 25: the Environment (Protection) Rules and the EIA Notification issued under this Act are precisely where the requirement of public consultation and the manner of conducting a public hearing are prescribed, and Section 19 lets any citizen prosecute after 60 days' notice. Runner-up is B (2 only), which would win on a strict reading that the bare text of the Act nowhere uses the words 'public participation' and that the procedure appears only in subordinate legislation. answers.reasoning: Schedule I of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016 prescribes precise siting criteria — minimum distances from rivers, ponds, highways, habitations, and a 20 km separation from airports and airbases, along with buffer-zone and no-development requirements — so option C is correct. Option A is wrong because the Rules require segregation into three streams (biodegradable, non-biodegradable or dry, and domestic hazardous waste), not five. Option B is wrong because the word 'only' excludes the many other areas the 2016 Rules brought in for the first time, including census towns, notified areas, railway and airport premises, ports, defence establishments, SEZs and places of pilgrimage. answers.value: Both are correct — fixed-term employment makes it easier for firms to shed workers, and no notice of termination is required for a temporary workman
answers.reasoning: The Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Central (Amendment) Rules, 2018 extended fixed-term employment to all sectors; a fixed-term contract simply lapses on expiry, which is not treated as retrenchment, so the employer escapes the notice, compensation and prior-permission requirements of the Industrial Disputes Act — statement 1 is therefore correct as an effect of the rules. The Model Standing Orders provide that no notice of termination is necessary in the case of a temporary workman, whether monthly rated, weekly rated or piece rated, so statement 2 is correct. Runner-up is B (2 only), which would win if statement 1 is rejected as an editorial inference about consequences rather than a provision of the Rules themselves.

answers.value: The Lead Bank Scheme
answers.reasoning: The Service Area Approach was introduced by the Reserve Bank of India in 1989 as part of the Lead Bank Scheme, assigning each rural and semi-urban bank branch a specific cluster of villages for planned credit deployment and orderly area development. It is a banking-sector credit-planning device, unconnected with the Integrated Rural Development Programme's asset-subsidy design, with MGNREGS's employment guarantee, or with the National Skill Development Mission.

answers.value: Only statements 1 and 3 are correct — sand is a minor mineral and States can frame anti-illegal-mining rules, but rule-making for minor minerals rests with the States, not the Centre

Section 15 vests in the State Governments the power to make rules for regulating the grant of quarry leases, mining leases and other mineral concessions in respect of minor minerals, so statement 2 is false — it reverses the actual allocation. Section 23C empowers State Governments to frame rules to prevent illegal mining, transportation and storage of minerals, so statement 3 is true. Of the two options excluding the false statement 2, only A also carries the true statement 1.

answers.value: Neither statement is correct — most of India's external debt is non-government, and it is denominated in several currencies besides the US dollar
answers.reasoning: Sovereign or government external debt is only about a fifth of India's total external debt; the bulk is non-government commercial borrowings, NRI deposits and short-term trade credit, so statement 1 is false. India's external debt is denominated in a basket of currencies — the US dollar is the largest share at roughly half, but the Indian rupee, SDR, Japanese yen and euro all account for meaningful portions — so the absolute claim in statement 2 is false. With both wrong, the answer is D.

answers.value: Deposits, which are a liability of the bank and not an asset
answers.reasoning: A commercial bank's balance sheet places deposits on the liabilities side, because they are money the bank owes to its customers and must repay on demand or at maturity. Advances (loans made), investments (securities held) and money at call and short notice (very short-term lending in the money market) are all claims the bank holds against others, so all three are assets. The odd one out is therefore deposits.

answers.value: Only 1 and 3 — IT export earnings and remittances both bring in foreign exchange and cushion the currency; higher government expenditure does not
answers.reasoning: A currency crisis becomes less likely when a country has steady, non-debt-creating inflows of foreign exchange to cover its external obligations. India's software and IT services exports and inward remittances from Indians abroad are exactly such inflows, and both are the classic offsets to India's merchandise trade deficit, so statements 1 and 3 are contributors. Increasing government expenditure widens the fiscal deficit and, through higher demand for imports, tends to worsen the current account and weaken the currency, so statement 2 works in the opposite direction.

answers.value: The Sarkaria Commission
answers.reasoning: The Sarkaria Commission on Centre-State Relations laid down four qualifications for a Governor in almost these words: he should be an eminent person in some walk of life, a person from outside the State, a detached figure not too intimately connected with the local politics of the State, and a person who has not taken too great a part in politics generally and particularly in the recent past. The stem reproduces this formulation, so the attribution is to Sarkaria rather than to the First Administrative Reforms Commission, the Rajamannar Committee (a Tamil Nadu State committee focused on greater State autonomy) or the NCRWC.

answers.value: Participatory Notes
answers.reasoning: Participatory Notes, or P-Notes, are offshore derivative instruments issued by SEBI-registered foreign portfolio investors against underlying Indian securities, allowing overseas investors to take exposure to Indian stocks without themselves registering with SEBI. A Certificate of Deposit is a negotiable money-market instrument issued by banks, Commercial Paper is an unsecured short-term instrument issued by corporates, and a Promissory Note is a general debt instrument — none of them is an offshore route into the Indian equity market.

answers.value: Only statement 1 is correct — CAMPA exists at both national and State levels, but the Act does not make people's participation mandatory
answers.reasoning: The Compensatory Afforestation Fund Act, 2016 provides for a National Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority and a State authority in every State and Union Territory, so statement 1 is correct. The Act and its Rules contain no mandatory requirement of people's participation, and the absence of any gram sabha consent or community-participation obligation — despite the Forest Rights Act — has been one of the principal criticisms of the legislation, so statement 2 is false.

answers.value: Only 1 and 2 — ad hoc parliamentary committees and the department-related standing committees
answers.reasoning: Independent sectoral regulators such as TRAI, IRDAI and the electricity regulatory commissions are accountable to Parliament, which scrutinises them through the department-related standing committees attached to the relevant ministries and, where needed, through ad hoc committees constituted for a specific inquiry. The Finance Commission is a constitutional body confined to recommending the distribution of tax revenues between the Union and the States, and NITI Aayog is a policy think tank with no review mandate over regulators; the Financial Sector Legislative Reforms Commission was a one-time body that examined only financial-sector laws, not telecom or electricity. Every option other than A includes at least one of these three.

answers.value: Only statements 1 and 2 are correct — the Second Plan pushed basic and capital goods and the Fourth Plan targeted concentration of economic power; the Fifth Plan claim about the financial sector is wrong
answers.reasoning: The Second Five-Year Plan, built on the Mahalanobis model, made a deliberate push towards heavy, basic and capital goods industries and towards import substitution in those goods, so statement 1 is correct. The Fourth Plan (1969-74) set out growth with stability and progressive self-reliance and explicitly sought to check the concentration of wealth and economic power — the MRTP Act of 1969 belongs to this period — so statement 2 is correct. The Fifth Plan (1974-79) was framed around removal of poverty and attainment of self-reliance, not around bringing the financial sector into the Plan for the first time, so statement 3 is false. Runner-up is D, which would win if statement 3 is accepted; a reviewer should check the Fifth Plan's stated objectives against that claim.

answers.value: Only statement 1 is correct — AIIB's membership exceeds 80, but China and not India is the largest shareholder, and AIIB has many non-regional members
answers.reasoning: AIIB grew from 57 founding members in 2016 to well over 80 approved members by 2019, so statement 1 is correct. China is by far the largest shareholder with roughly a quarter to a third of the voting power; India is the second largest, so statement 2 is false. AIIB deliberately admits non-regional members, and the United Kingdom, Germany, France, Canada and others from outside Asia are members, so statement 3 is false. Since statements 2 and 3 are both false, every option except A is eliminated regardless of how strictly statement 1 is read.

answers.value: To speed up resolution of stressed assets of Rs 50 crore or more held under consortium or multiple-banking arrangements
answers.reasoning: The Inter-Creditor Agreement of 2018 flowed from the Sunil Mehta Committee's Project Sashakt proposals. It binds the lenders in a consortium to a common framework in which a resolution plan approved by lenders holding a specified majority of the outstanding exposure becomes binding on all, so that a single dissenting bank can no longer stall resolution of a large stressed account. It has nothing to do with the fiscal or current account deficit, with financing government infrastructure projects, or with acting as a regulator over loan applications.

answers.value: The Banks Board Bureau
answers.reasoning: The Banks Board Bureau, set up in 2016 on the recommendation of the P. J. Nayak Committee, is the body that recommends candidates for appointment as whole-time directors and non-executive chairmen of public sector banks and financial institutions, and advises on their governance. The Reserve Bank of India is the banking regulator but does not select PSB chairmen, the Finance Ministry acts on the Bureau's recommendations rather than making the selection itself, and the management of a bank cannot appoint its own chairman.

answers.value: Only statements 2 and 3 are correct — PNGRB promotes competitive gas markets and appeals from it lie to the Appellate Tribunal for Electricity, but it is not India's first regulator
answers.reasoning: PNGRB was constituted under the Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board Act, 2006 and began functioning in 2007; SEBI (1992), TRAI (1997) and the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (1998) all predate it, so statement 1 is false. The Act's preamble and Section 11 charge the Board with protecting consumer interests and ensuring competitive markets for petroleum, petroleum products and natural gas, so statement 2 is true. Section 33 of the Act makes the Appellate Tribunal for Electricity the appellate authority against PNGRB's orders, so statement 3 is true. Only option B excludes the false statement 1 while keeping both true ones.

answers.value: Neither statement states a real difference — LTE is marketed as 4G, not 3G, and VoLTE is not a voice-only technology
answers.reasoning: LTE is universally marketed as 4G and VoLTE as an enhancement over 4G, not as 3G and advanced 3G, so statement 1 is false. LTE is indeed an all-IP, packet-switched data-bearing technology, but VoLTE is not voice-only: it carries voice as packets over that same LTE data network and lets voice and high-speed data run simultaneously on the same connection, which is precisely its advantage over circuit-switched fallback. Since the second half of statement 2 is wrong, the statement as a whole fails, and neither point survives.

answers.value: Only statement 3 is correct — a woman who already has two surviving children gets reduced maternity leave; the leave split and the number of creche visits are both misstated
answers.reasoning: The Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017 grants 26 weeks of paid leave of which not more than 8 weeks may be taken before the expected date of delivery, so the symmetrical 'three months before and three months after' in statement 1 is wrong. The Act requires an establishment with a creche to allow the mother four visits a day, including the rest interval, not six, so statement 2 is wrong. A woman who already has two or more surviving children is entitled to only 12 weeks, of which not more than 6 weeks may be pre-delivery, so statement 3 is correct. Only option C names statement 3 alone.

answers.value: Maintenance of law and order, which is not one of the Doing Business indicators
answers.reasoning: The World Bank's Ease of Doing Business Index is built from ten indicator sets: starting a business, dealing with construction permits, getting electricity, registering property, getting credit, protecting minority investors, paying taxes, trading across borders, enforcing contracts and resolving insolvency. Paying taxes, registering property and dealing with construction permits are all on that list. Law and order is a governance measure captured by other indices such as the Worldwide Governance Indicators, not by Doing Business.

answers.value: The e-Waste (Management and Handling) Rules, 2011
answers.reasoning: Extended Producer Responsibility — the principle that a producer's responsibility for a product extends to its environmentally sound end-of-life management — entered Indian law with the e-Waste (Management and Handling) Rules, 2011, which defined the term and placed collection and channelisation duties on producers of electrical and electronic equipment. The Bio-medical Waste Rules of 1998 place the duty on the occupier of the health-care facility, the Recycled Plastic Rules of 1999 dealt with the thickness and specifications of plastic carry bags, and the Food Safety and Standards Regulations of 2011 concern food safety, not waste take-back.

answers.value: Procurement incidentals and distribution cost, added to MSP and bonus
answers.reasoning: FCI's economic cost has three components: the minimum support price with any bonus paid to farmers, the procurement incidentals (mandi charges, commission, bagging, transport to the depot and the like), and the distribution cost (freight, handling, storage and interest charges, and administrative overheads) incurred until the grain reaches the fair price shops. MSP plus procurement incidentals gives the acquisition cost, and adding distribution cost gives the economic cost. Options A and B name only one element each, and option D captures only godown charges rather than the whole distribution cost.

answers.value: The level of mutual trust and harmony in the society
answers.reasoning: Social capital refers to the networks, shared norms, trust and cooperation among people that let a society function collectively — it is a property of relationships, not of individuals or of things. The proportion of literates and the working-age population are measures of human capital and of the labour force, while the stock of buildings, infrastructure and machines is physical capital. Only mutual trust and harmony belongs to the social dimension.

answers.value: Neither statement is correct — High Courts can strike down central laws, and the Supreme Court can review constitutional amendments
answers.reasoning: Under Article 226 and the general power of judicial review, a High Court can examine and declare unconstitutional any law, central or State, that violates the Constitution, so statement 1 is false. Since Kesavananda Bharati the Supreme Court has held that a constitutional amendment can be struck down if it damages the basic structure of the Constitution, and it has actually done so, notably in Minerva Mills and in the case invalidating the NJAC amendment, so statement 2 is false. Both being wrong, the answer is D.

answers.value: Only statement 1 is correct — PPP rates do come from comparing an identical basket of goods, but in PPP terms India is the third largest economy, not the sixth
answers.reasoning: Purchasing power parity exchange rates are computed precisely by pricing an identical basket of goods and services in different countries and asking how much local currency buys what one dollar buys in the United States, so statement 1 is correct. Measured in PPP dollars India ranks third in the world after China and the United States; the sixth place belongs to India's ranking in nominal market-exchange-rate GDP around this period, so statement 2 confuses the two measures and is false.

answers.value: Only statements 1 and 3 are correct — rice has the largest kharif area and cotton exceeds sugarcane, but jowar is far below oilseeds and sugarcane area has not steadily fallen
answers.reasoning: Rice occupies roughly 40 million hectares and is comfortably the largest kharif crop by area, so statement 1 is correct. Kharif oilseeds, dominated by soybean and groundnut, cover about 18 million hectares against only a few million hectares under jowar, so statement 2 is false. Cotton at around 12 million hectares far exceeds sugarcane at around 5 million hectares, so statement 3 is correct. Sugarcane area has fluctuated up and down over the period rather than declining steadily, so statement 4 is false. Only option A carries exactly 1 and 3.

answers.value: Vegetable oils, India's largest agricultural import by value
answers.reasoning: India meets well over half its edible oil demand through imports of palm, soybean and sunflower oil, and the annual bill runs to roughly ten billion dollars — several times the value of any other farm import. Pulses imports peaked at only a few billion dollars and fell sharply after the domestic production recovery and the imposition of quantitative limits; fresh fruits and spices are smaller still, and India is in fact a large net exporter of spices.

answers.value: Opportunity to develop oneself fully
answers.reasoning: In political theory the positive and most complete conception of liberty, associated with Laski and the idealist tradition, is the maintenance of conditions in which people have the opportunity to be their best selves and develop their personality fully. Absence of restraint is only the negative half of the idea, protection against tyranny names one condition for liberty rather than liberty itself, and the opportunity to do whatever one likes describes licence, which political theory expressly distinguishes from liberty.

answers.value: Following an expansionary monetary policy, which would weaken rather than support the rupee
answers.reasoning: An expansionary monetary policy lowers interest rates and expands money supply, narrowing the return differential that attracts foreign capital and encouraging outflows, so it pushes the rupee down rather than arresting its slide; a central bank defending a currency normally tightens instead. The other three are standard defensive measures: curbing non-essential imports and pushing exports narrows the current account deficit, rupee-denominated Masala Bonds bring in foreign capital while shifting exchange-rate risk to the overseas investor, and easing external commercial borrowing norms encourages dollar inflows.

answers.value: Only statement 1 is correct — the data must be stored in a system only in India; there is no public-ownership requirement and the audit report goes to the RBI, not the CAG
answers.reasoning: The RBI's April 2018 circular on Storage of Payment System Data directs all payment system providers to ensure that the entire data relating to payment systems operated by them is stored in a system only in India, which is exactly statement 1. Nothing in the directive requires the systems to be owned or operated by public sector enterprises — it applies to private and foreign operators alike — so statement 2 is false. The circular requires a System Audit Report by a CERT-In empanelled auditor to be submitted to the Reserve Bank of India, not to the Comptroller and Auditor General, so statement 3 is false.

answers.value: The European Union
answers.reasoning: The General Data Protection Regulation was adopted by the European Union in April 2016 and became enforceable across the Union on 25 May 2018 after a two-year transition. It is an EU regulation with extraterritorial reach over anyone processing the personal data of EU residents. Australia relies on its Privacy Act, Canada on PIPEDA, and the United States has no single federal data protection statute of this kind.

answers.value: Russia — the nuclear action plan was signed with Russia at the annual bilateral summit
answers.reasoning: The 'Action Plan for Prioritization and Implementation of Cooperation Areas in the Nuclear Field' was signed between India and Russia at the annual bilateral summit in October 2018, alongside the wider India-Russia civil nuclear partnership that covers the Kudankulam units and cooperation in third countries. India's nuclear engagement with Japan runs through the 2016 civil nuclear cooperation agreement, with the United States through the 2008 123 Agreement, and with the United Kingdom through a separate civil nuclear declaration — none of them under this title.

answers.value: An increase in the banking habit of the population
answers.reasoning: The money multiplier rises when a larger share of money is held as bank deposits rather than as currency, because deposits can be lent on and re-deposited while cash held outside the banking system cannot. A stronger banking habit lowers the currency-to-deposit ratio and therefore raises the multiplier. Raising the cash reserve ratio or the statutory liquidity ratio locks up a larger fraction of deposits and lowers the multiplier, and the mere size of the population has no bearing on it.

answers.value: Only statements 3 and 4 are correct — statements 1 and 2 have the definitions of AR and VR swapped
answers.reasoning: Statement 1 describes a fully simulated environment that shuts out the physical world, which is Virtual Reality and not Augmented Reality, so it is false. Statement 2 describes computer-generated images overlaid on real objects and surroundings, which is Augmented Reality and not Virtual Reality, so it is also false — the item has deliberately transposed the two. Statement 3 correctly describes AR as keeping the user in the real world and enhancing it through a phone or PC camera, and statement 4 correctly describes VR as closing off the world and transposing the user into a fully immersive one. Only option B names exactly 3 and 4.

answers.value: An early human species
answers.reasoning: Denisovans are an extinct group of archaic humans identified from fragmentary remains and ancient DNA recovered from Denisova Cave in the Altai Mountains of Siberia, and later from a jawbone on the Tibetan Plateau. They were a sister population to the Neanderthals and interbred with modern humans, leaving traces in the genomes of present-day Melanesian and other populations. The term has nothing to do with dinosaurs, with any cave system in North-East India, or with a geological period.

answers.value: The claim that functional chromosomes can be created by joining DNA segments taken from cells of different species is the odd one out
answers.reasoning: Options B, C and D describe long-established laboratory routines: synthetic oligonucleotides and whole synthetic genes are chemically manufactured, the polymerase chain reaction replicates DNA entirely outside any living cell, and plant and animal tissue culture makes cells divide in petri dishes. That leaves A as the statement the item treats as false, on the view that a chromosome needs species-matched centromere and telomere sequences to segregate correctly and cannot simply be stitched together from another species' DNA. The runner-up here is not a rival letter but the possibility that the item is defective: yeast and human artificial chromosomes are in fact chimeric constructs that carry inserts from other species and do function as chromosomes, so A has a defensible reading as true, and if that reading is taken the question has no incorrect option at all. A reviewer should test that, not look for a different letter — B, C and D are each routine, unambiguous laboratory practice, so no other option can be the intended answer.

answers.value: All three statements are correct descriptions of a digital signature
answers.reasoning: A digital signature does serve as proof of identity when accessing information or a server online, and it is an electronic method of signing a document that simultaneously guarantees the content has not been altered since signing, since any change breaks the hash — statements 2 and 3 are plainly correct. Statement 1 rests on the fact that a digital signature under the Information Technology Act is an electronic record which travels with a Digital Signature Certificate naming the Certifying Authority that issued it, so the signature does identify its issuing authority. Runner-up is B (2 and 3 only), which wins if the setter insists on the strict distinction that it is the Digital Signature Certificate, not the signature itself, that identifies the Certifying Authority. [Answer corrected to C from the official UPSC answer key; an independent blind derivation had reached D. The reasoning above argues for D and is retained so the disagreement is visible rather than hidden.]

answers.value: All three — wearables locate a person, monitor sleep and assist the hearing impaired
answers.reasoning: GPS-enabled smartwatches and trackers identify a wearer's location and are routinely used for exactly that purpose. Fitness bands and smartwatches track sleep duration and sleep stages using accelerometers and heart-rate sensors. Hearing aids and cochlear-implant processors are themselves wearable devices, and modern smart hearing aids stream and amplify sound for the hearing impaired. All three tasks are therefore accomplished by wearable devices.

answers.value: Statements 1, 2 and 4 — gene silencing, cancer therapy and virus-resistant crops; RNAi has no role in hormone replacement
answers.reasoning: RNA interference works by using small interfering or micro RNAs to degrade or block the translation of a target messenger RNA, so it is inherently a gene-silencing tool — statement 1 is its defining application. Silencing oncogenes and other genes driving tumour growth is an active line of cancer therapeutics, so statement 2 holds. RNAi-based virus resistance has been engineered into crops, the papaya ringspot-virus-resistant papaya being the standard example, so statement 4 holds. Hormone replacement therapy supplies a deficient hormone from outside and has nothing to do with silencing a transcript, so statement 3 fails, which rules out options B and C; option D omits the true statement 2.

answers.value: Gravitational waves were detected
answers.reasoning: Black hole mergers are observed not by light but by the ripples in spacetime they radiate, which the LIGO and Virgo interferometers detect as minute changes in the length of their arms — the first such detection, GW150914, came from two merging black holes over a billion light-years away. Higgs boson detection is a particle-collider result from the LHC, wormhole travel remains entirely unconfirmed speculation, and while the merger involves singularities the observational significance of these events is the direct detection of gravitational waves.

answers.value: Only 2 and 3 — incorrect antibiotic dosing and antibiotic use in livestock farming
answers.reasoning: Multi-drug resistance arises in the pathogen population, through selection pressure that lets resistant strains survive and multiply. Incomplete or incorrect antibiotic courses leave partially susceptible organisms alive to be selected, and the routine use of antibiotics as growth promoters and prophylactics in livestock creates a large reservoir of resistant bacteria that reaches humans through food and the environment — so statements 2 and 3 are genuine causes. A human being's genetic make-up does not alter the bacterium's resistance genes, so statement 1 is false, and the mere presence of multiple chronic diseases is a risk factor for infection rather than a cause of resistance in the microbe, so statement 4 is false.

answers.value: A molecular scissors used in targeted gene editing
answers.reasoning: Cas9 is a CRISPR-associated endonuclease that is guided by a short RNA sequence to a matching site in the genome, where it cuts both strands of the DNA so that the break can be repaired in a way that disables or replaces the target gene. It is therefore accurately described as molecular scissors for targeted gene editing. It is not a diagnostic biosensor in itself, not a plant pest-resistance gene like the Bt cry genes, and not a herbicide.

answers.value: The claim that Hepatitis B has no vaccine while Hepatitis C does is wrong — it is the other way round
answers.reasoning: A safe and effective vaccine against Hepatitis B has existed for decades and is part of India's universal immunisation programme, whereas no licensed vaccine exists against Hepatitis C, which is treated instead with direct-acting antiviral drugs. Option B inverts this and is therefore the incorrect statement. The other three are accurate: Hepatitis B shares HIV's routes of transmission through blood, sexual contact and mother to child; global infections with Hepatitis B and C run to hundreds of millions against a few tens of millions living with HIV; and both hepatitis infections are often silent for years before liver damage appears.
